title: Jobsite Safety Orientation
short_answer: PPE, ladders and lifts, dust and silica on our everyday tasks, and the hard stops where the right move is to put the tools down.
summary: PPE, ladders and lifts, dust and silica on our everyday tasks, and the hard stops where the right move is to put the tools down.
plain_words: This is not a full OSHA program — it is the field card. Wear the right PPE for the task, do not climb what you are not cleared for, control dust when you cut or sand, and stop when you hit asbestos/lead/structure/unknown material. Speed never wins against a hospital bill or a failed inspection.
when_to_use: Every job, every day — onboarding and refreshers
Before demo, sanding, grinding, or overhead ACT work
When access, scaffold, or material stops look wrong
prerequisites: Site-specific PPE rules from the GC
Lift/scaffold authorization per Job Start and GC policy

tools.name: Dust mask or respirator when cutting/sanding creates fines
Vacuum-sanded or shrouded tools where Table 1 applies

steps.body: Three points of contact on ladders. Face the ladder. Do not carry a full sheet up a step ladder — stage material first or use the right equipment.
Scaffold matches the Job Start note. Missing planks, missing rails, or "we'll just use it for a minute" = stop and call the lead.
Lifts only with a ticket / authorization the GC and GVC accept. No borrowed keys, no "I watched someone."
Refuse unsafe access. You will not get in trouble for refusing a bad ladder. You will for falling off one.

warnings.title: Hard stops — put the tools down
warnings.body: Pre-1981 material without a survey (presume PACM). Pre-1978 housing / child-occupied lead rules. Anything structural you were not told to cut. Untraceable conduit or live unknowns. Stop → call the lead → do not resume until someone with authority says so. Recognizing that a decision is required is the skill — not deciding asbestos yourself.

warnings.title: PPE by task (minimums)
warnings.body: Hang/cut board: eye protection; gloves when carrying; dust mask or respirator when cutting creates fines. Pole/power sand: eye protection; vacuum collection preferred; respirator when Table 1 controls are not met. Grind bead/cut steel: eye/face, hearing, gloves; silica controls on concrete/masonry. ACT/overhead: eye protection; hard hat where required; secure footing before looking up. Demo: full site PPE plus Demolition hard stops — read that page before starting.

experts.tag: Full detail · dust & silica on our work
experts.summary: OSHA's silica rule is not only for knocking out concrete. Cutting board, grinding compound, and power sanding generate respirable dust. Table 1 gives task-based controls (continuous water or vacuum collection for many grinding tasks) — implementing the listed control for that tool is compliance without inventing your own plan. Prefer vacuum sanding and shrouded tools over open dry sanding in occupied or multi-trade spaces. Do not dust out a room with a leaf blower. Respirator fit testing and a written program belong to the office — field improvisation is not a substitute when the task requires a respirator. Deeper demo / ACM / lead stops live on Demolition.

quality_checks.prompt: PPE matches the task (eyes, dust, hearing as required)
Ladder/scaffold/lift access refused or corrected when unsafe
Hard-stop conditions escalated to lead before work resumes

common_mistakes.title: Carrying board up a step ladder
common_mistakes.wrong: One person, full sheet, three-point contact broken
common_mistakes.right: Stage material or use lift/scaffold built for the load

common_mistakes.title: Open dry sanding in occupied space
common_mistakes.wrong: No vacuum or shroud when Table 1 requires it
common_mistakes.right: Vacuum sanding or listed silica control for the tool
common_mistakes.why: Silica exposure to crew and other trades

common_mistakes.title: Guessing on PACM or lead
common_mistakes.wrong: Cut or sand pre-1981 / pre-1978 material without a stop
common_mistakes.right: Stop, call the lead, wait for authority
common_mistakes.why: Regulatory and health exposure — not a field call
